reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate rather than writing new weekend logic, and all three existing callers are routed through it.

duplication.why: The skip-vs-move rule is in one function, but the 'daily + skipWeekend means look further ahead' logic is re-derived separately in getNextDate (take = LOOKAHEAD) and getUpcomingDates (count * LOOKAHEAD + filter + slice), and each caller keeps its own skipWeekend ternary.

placement.why: The rule lives in the shared schedules module next to the existing weekend helper; frequency is carried in the rschedule data in rule-utils where weekendSolve already is.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, its three call sites, the data plumbing and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: A nullable return plus caller-side lookahead and null filtering, and a convoluted loop condition in schedule-template (nextDate == null ? nextBaseDate < nextMonth : ...), make the semantics easy to break; an occurrence-iterator helper would be cleaner.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily lookahead handling reshaped in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate (take = DAILY_WEEKEND_LOOKAHEAD) and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates (take: count * DAILY_WEEKEND_LOOKAHEAD, filter null, slice)

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getDateWithSkippedWeekend decides skip (daily) vs move for every caller (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, schedule-template)
